scenario_text: Increase memory on a supported application server after the application owner confirms the change window and the platform has available capacity.
Install an operating-system release that is outside the agency's supported standard because a vendor says its application will not run on the supported version.
Reset a user's password after identity verification using the approved service-desk process.
Disable multi-factor authentication for an application because several users are having difficulty completing the second factor.
Run the scheduled quarterly restore test for a non-critical server using the documented recovery procedure.
Reduce database backup retention from 90 days to 14 days to save storage, without confirming records-retention or business requirements.
Confirm that a bidder included the required support term and response-time commitment stated in the solicitation.
Accept a hosted vendor solution that stores agency data outside the United States because its price is substantially lower than competing bids.
Add monitoring for CPU, memory, and disk utilization on an existing supported server using the agency's standard monitoring platform and alert thresholds.
Disable application health checks in the load balancer because one server is intermittently failing the checks and being removed from service.
Enable standard operating-system audit logging on a newly deployed server using the approved logging baseline and forward logs to the existing logging platform.
Ignore repeated endpoint alerts from one executive workstation because the user reports that the computer is working normally.
Verify that the immutable backup copy for a protected workload is still within the approved retention period and passes the platform's integrity check.
Promise business leadership a one-hour recovery point for a critical application even though backups currently run every eight hours and no additional replication is configured.
Ask a bidder to clarify which supported operating-system versions are included in its proposal because the response lists only a product family.
Approve a proposal that depends on an unsupported version of the agency's database platform because replacing the database would increase the vendor's implementation cost.
Apply an approved firmware update to a storage controller using the vendor procedure during a scheduled maintenance window.
Combine production and test workloads on the same storage volumes to avoid purchasing additional capacity, even though the current design separates them.
Remove an expired temporary administrator account after confirming the associated maintenance work is complete.
Allow a system administrator to use a personal email account to receive security alerts because the agency mailbox is difficult to access after hours.
Review a weekly backup-failure report and rerun a failed job after correcting a documented credential issue.
Change the recovery plan to restore only the application server and omit its external database dependency to shorten the documented recovery time.
Confirm that a proposed product supports the operating-system versions listed as mandatory in the solicitation.
Waive the requirement for audit-log export because the preferred product can only retain logs inside the vendor's cloud portal.

A supported server requires a memory increase that is already covered by the approved capacity plan, but the change must occur during a narrow maintenance window because another service depends on it.
A development workload must be moved to another approved cluster because the current cluster is being retired under an existing migration plan.
A replacement network device is functionally similar to the current one but uses a different operating system and management model not yet supported by staff tools.
A new server is requested in the production environment, but the application owner cannot identify backup, monitoring, authentication, or recovery requirements.
A vulnerability scanner reports a medium finding that matches a known accepted vendor configuration, and the approved procedure requires documenting and monitoring it.
A workstation triggers a suspicious-process alert, but the security platform automatically blocks the process and the runbook defines the validation steps.
A server has a critical vulnerability, but remediation requires changing an application component that has not been tested by the vendor.
A business application cannot meet one current hardening requirement, but the vendor offers a compensating configuration that is not part of the agency baseline.
An application owner asks for a one-time restore to a test environment using an existing isolated recovery network and approved access controls.
A business system is moved to a different server, but its recovery tier, retention, and backup schedule remain unchanged and documented.
A critical system is added to backup, but the owner asks to skip replication until bandwidth is upgraded sometime next year.
The team proposes keeping the backup console permanently logged in on a shared operations workstation to speed emergency restores.
A bidder omits a model number for a network adapter, and procurement requests clarification to verify compatibility with the published specification.
A vendor asks whether a required reporting format can be delivered through the already approved secure file-transfer method instead of email.
The project team wants to accept a lower backup-retention commitment from the vendor because all other technical scores are high.
A vendor asks to substitute a different identity platform after award because its original integration estimate was too low.
